chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Sulayman ibn Sama'a, from al-Hazza', from his uncle Asim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Women are four (types) — an all-encompassing good, and a fruitful spring, and a careless destructive one, and a lice-ridden shackle.'

key_terms.جَامِعٌ مُجْمِعٌ: all-encompassing good — a woman who brings together virtues and unites the family
key_terms.خَرْقَاءُ مُقْمِعٌ: careless and destructive — a foolish woman who ruins her household
key_terms.رَبِيعٌ مُرْبِعٌ: fruitful spring — a woman who bears children and brings prosperity
key_terms.غُلٌّ قَمِلٌ: lice-ridden shackle — a woman who is a burdensome affliction, oppressive like iron fetters infested with vermin

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of women mentioned by the Prophet Muhammad in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (saww) categorized women into four rhetorical types using vivid metaphorical language: the first two are praiseworthy (all-encompassing goodness and fruitful abundance), while the last two are cautionary (careless and destructive, and an oppressive burden). This typology, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (as), was understood in classical Islamic discourse as guidance for men in choosing a spouse, expressed in compact Arabic rhyming pairs (saj') characteristic of prophetic eloquence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Suleyman Bin Sama’at, from Al Haza’a, from his uncle Aasim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The women are four (types) – An all inclusive goodness, and a child-bearing fountain, and a careless destructive one, and a feed for parasite’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Safmah ibn al-Khattab from Sulayman ibn Sama‘ah from al-Hadhdha’ from his uncle, ‘Asem who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ’Women are of four kinds: Goodness in all respects, a child bearing fountain, a dimwitted destructive one and feed for parasites.”’
